To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of protein synthesis in monkey fibroblasts is regulated at the level of translation and that this regulation involves a shift of polyadenylated mRNA from a polysomal location in exponential phase cells to a postpolysomal location in stationary phase cells.

the nonpolysome polyadenylated mRNA of stationary phase monkey cells is fully capable of serving as a template in a wheat germ system and that this species of mRNA is not being translated because of an initiation block.

the nonpolysome-associated poly(A)-containing RNA in stationary phase cells has the structural properties of a messenger RNA, is fully capable, in vitro, of being translated, but is not translated in the cell due to the operation in the stationary phase cell of a translational block.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of protein synthesis in animal cells.
a novel species of polyadenylated mRNA that is found in stationary phase cells.
the regulation of the translation of mRNA during growth-related fluctuations in protein synthesis in animal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mRNA utilization pattern in stationary phase cells has been altered to a pattern in which the rate of translation of a specific set of mRNA's has been reduced to a level below the rate of mRNA degradation.

in stationary phase cells, a substantial fraction of the cytopl- ic polyadenylated mRNA is present in a post-polysomal location, and that this mRNA is fully capable of translation but is blocked in translation.

in stationary phase cells a large proportion of the polyadenylated messenger RNA is in the form of large polysomes and a large proportion of polyadenylated mRNA is in the form or small polysomes or is not in polysomes at all, but is still in the form of polyribosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of protein synthesis in animal cells is controlled at the translational level by a mechanism that involves a block in translational initiation.
the rate of protein synthesis is regulated in stationary phase cells by the rate of translation of a large pool of nontranslating mRNA.

the regulation of protein synthesis in stationary phase cells involves a decrease in the number of ribosomes engaged in translation and an accumulation of a species of nonpolysome-bound polyadenylated mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant pool of polyadenylated mRNA in stationary phase monkey cells that is not being utilized in protein synthesis.
the translational machinery of the cell is highly sensitive to changes in the growth state of the cell.
the translational initiation machinery is not fully active during the stationary phase of growth.
